textbook:
Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE ACROCENTRIC METAPHASE CHROMOSOME (shaped like human chromosome 13, 14, 21 or 22), centred in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space, filling the whole square edge-to-edge on a neutral dark-charcoal background with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox. Match a refined educational plate: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette, THIN clean outlines, gentle soft shading.

SHAPE, MOST IMPORTANT INSTRUCTION: picture the letter "Y" turned upside down, or a wishbone. Near the VERY TOP of the shape there is only a tiny pair of stub arms, each stub shorter than the waist is wide — barely a bump, almost invisible nubs. From that same waist, a pair of very long arms sweeps DOWNWARD and spreads apart in a wide V, each long arm taking up nearly half the total height of the frame. The waist sits close to the TOP of the whole figure, not in the middle. Do NOT draw four arms of similar length under any circumstances — that is the wrong, generic answer. The correct silhouette looks lopsided: almost all the visual mass is BELOW the waist.

CENTROMERE: no separate inserted diamond/star/blob shape. The paired tubes physically narrow and pinch together like a cinched rope at the (near-top) waist, a single continuous hourglass outline, tinted warm terracotta (#C4685A) only as a colour change within that continuous outline. Two small gold (#E0A33E) kinetochore marks sit back-to-back right at the pinch.

EACH ARM IS TWO SEPARATE PARALLEL TUBES side by side with a visible gap the entire length of every arm — one tube per pair cool mid-blue (#7FA8CC), its twin the same blue one shade lighter (#A9C6E0), each chromatid keeping its own shade continuously from stub tip through the waist to the long tip.

Cap all four arm tips (both tiny stub tips and both long tips) with small rounded fresh-green (#6FBF8F) telomere caps, one per tube.

NO ENCLOSURE: no nuclear envelope, no round nucleus, no cell membrane anywhere.

PACKING-HIERARCHY SIDE SEQUENCE in the empty margin: three small plain pictograms left to right, connected by a thin line, NO letters/numbers/parentheses anywhere: (1) a multi-turn RIGHT-HANDED DNA double helix (3+ twists); (2) the same thread with violet (#B98FC4) beads strung on it; (3) a small loose tangled scribble.

Exactly ONE chromosome, no duplicates. ABSOLUTELY NO TEXT OF ANY KIND anywhere.
sem:
Photorealistic false-color scanning-electron-micrograph of a SINGLE ISOLATED ACROCENTRIC METAPHASE CHROMOSOME (shaped like human chromosome 13, 14, 21 or 22) resting on a subtly textured substrate, centred in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous margin, filling the whole square edge-to-edge with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox. Crisp high-contrast 3D surface relief typical of a true high-magnification SEM scan: the surface is ROUGH, KNOBBLY, almost coral-like or cauliflower-like with dense fine granular texture over its whole surface.

SHAPE, MOST IMPORTANT INSTRUCTION: picture the letter "Y" turned upside down, or a wishbone. Near the VERY TOP there is only a tiny pair of stub arms, each shorter than the waist is wide — barely a bump. From that same waist, a pair of very long arms sweeps DOWNWARD and spreads apart in a wide V, each taking up nearly half the total frame height. The waist sits close to the TOP of the whole figure, not the middle. Do NOT render four arms of similar length. Almost all the visual mass must be BELOW the waist.

STRUCTURE: two rough-textured chromatid lobes lie pressed together side by side along the full length of each arm — a shallow but visible groove runs between the two lobes for the ENTIRE length of every arm. They pinch into a shared, visibly NARROWER waist (the centromere) — a real constriction in the solid rough material, like a rope cinched tight, never a separate inserted blob. At the waist, a slightly raised, denser fibrous plate of surface texture on each chromatid (the kinetochore) faces outward on each side, back-to-back. All four arm tips (tiny stubs and long tips) taper to a slightly smoother, rounded cap (the telomeres).

False-colour palette: warm gold-tan surface tones with cooler shadowed crevices, false-colour surface only. Shallow depth of field, cool studio microscopy lighting. Exactly ONE isolated chromosome specimen, no duplicates, no debris. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks anywhere.
